question: Is it cheaper for a startup to self-host an open-source LLM or pay for cloud APIs?

input_check.reason: The request asks for a cost and architectural comparison between self-hosting and cloud APIs for startups.

plan.main_question: Is it cheaper for a startup to self-host an open-source LLM or pay for cloud APIs?
plan.decision_context: Startup leadership evaluating infrastructure and operational costs of running AI models versus paying per-token API fees.

decision.rationale: Market and technical specialists are needed to evaluate both the direct financial costs (hardware, APIs, break-even) and the engineering overhead associated with self-hosting versus commercial APIs.

summaries.sq1: On-demand rental for a single inference-class GPU ranges from $1.50 to $4.00 per hour across providers [ev8]. A single high-memory GPU can serve 7B-14B parameter models, while 70B-class models require two to four GPUs [ev9].
summaries.sq2: Small and mid-sized models are priced between $0.10 and $0.60 per million input tokens, while frontier models range from $2 to $15 per million input tokens [ev10]. Output tokens typically cost three to five times more than input tokens [ev11].
summaries.sq4: No verified evidence was directly extracted for the exact break-even monthly token volume under sq4, though supporting estimates are discussed elsewhere. Open issues: Could not extract specific numeric break-even token volume from the available sources.

summaries.sq3: Maintaining self-hosted LLM infrastructure requires significant engineering time for setup, monitoring, driver management, and tuning. Initial setup and autoscaling configuration can take several weeks of engineering effort [ev7]. Ongoing maintenance includes handling out-of-memory crashes under load [ev13], debugging driver and container issues causing downtime [ev12], and constant monitoring, which can overwhelm small startup teams without dedicated MLOps staff [ev14].

agreements: Self-hosting a mid-sized model has a break-even point compared to APIs between 1 and 3 billion tokens per month [ev3, ev4, ev5, ev6].

report.title: Cost Evaluation: Self-Hosting Open-Source LLMs Versus Cloud APIs for Startups
report.executive_summary: For startups with low to moderate token volumes, cloud APIs offer a lower total cost of ownership than self-hosting. Self-hosting open-source LLMs becomes more cost-effective only when monthly token volume reaches a break-even threshold between 1 and 3 billion tokens. This financial tipping point depends heavily on factoring in ongoing engineering labor costs for deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.

findings.statement: Running a single inference-class GPU around the clock on-demand costs roughly $1,100 to $2,900 per month before storage, networking, and monitoring, with hourly rates ranging from $1.50 to $4.00.
A single high-memory GPU comfortably serves a 7 to 14B parameter model, whereas 70B-class models require two to four GPUs, multiplying monthly costs.
Frontier model APIs are priced between $2 and $15 per million input tokens, with output tokens typically costing three to five times more than input tokens.
Keeping a self-hosted model reliable in production for organizations with fewer than ten engineers requires between 0.25 and 0.5 of a full-time engineer on an ongoing basis.
Initial setup of serving, autoscaling, monitoring, and upgrades takes about three weeks of engineering time.
The break-even point for self-hosting a mid-sized model compared to cloud API prices falls between 1 and 3 billion tokens per month.

limitations: Evidence relies primarily on general blogs, academic modeling for small engineering teams, and forum anecdotes, lacking direct proprietary startup internal cost audits.
Specific networking, storage, and precise multi-region latency overheads are not fully quantified in the provided data.
report.recommendation: Use commercial cloud APIs if your monthly token volume is below 1 billion tokens. Revisit self-hosting open-source LLMs only when your application scales past 1 to 3 billion tokens per month and you have allocated 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer for ongoing MLOps maintenance.
